sessions.title: First lesson
turns: Hi! I'm Mina. I'm learning Japanese, about a year in. I want to pass the JLPT N4 in December.
Welcome, Mina! N4 in December is a good target. What do you find hardest so far?
Keigo, honestly. Polite and honorific forms fall apart the moment I have to speak. I freeze.
That's very common. We can put a short keigo drill into every session so it becomes automatic.
Yes please, every session. Also some context: I'm moving to Osaka for work next spring.
Exciting! Then everyday Osaka situations will make good practice material.
Exactly. Shops, the ward office, the train. That's what I'll actually face.
Noted. Today let's practise asking for things politely in a shop: kudasai versus itadakemasu ka.
Itadakemasu ka always feels too long, but okay. Can you add romaji under new kanji? I read kana fine but kanji slows me down.
Sure. I'll keep kana as is and add romaji under any new kanji.

sessions.title: Ward office role-play
turns: Can we role-play the ward office? I need to register my address when I arrive in Osaka.
Of course. I'll be the clerk. Start by saying you'd like to register a change of address.
Tenshutodoke wo dashitai desu. Is that polite enough?
It works. More polite: tenshutodoke wo teishutsu shitai no desu ga. Clerks will use sonkeigo with you, so listen for irasshaimase and o-machi kudasai.
Okay, that sonkeigo part is exactly what loses me. Keep pushing me on it.
Will do. Your particles were clean today; the keigo is the only real gap.
Ten minutes is about my limit on weeknights, by the way. I study after work.
Then weeknight sessions stay at ten to fifteen minutes, one keigo drill plus one situation.
Perfect. And I like it when you correct me straight away rather than at the end.
Understood: corrections inline, as soon as I see them.

sessions.title: Train announcements
turns: Today I want listening practice. Osaka train announcements, like on the Midosuji line.
Good choice. Announcements are full of keigo: mamonaku, go-chui kudasai, o-noriase shimasu.
O-noriase shimasu is humble form, right? The railway lowering itself?
Exactly, kenjougo. You are getting faster at spotting it.
My N4 mock score went up to 112 out of 180. The reading section is still the weakest.
That's a pass on the mock. For reading, we can add one short passage per session.
Only if it's about Osaka life. Generic textbook passages bore me.
Osaka passages only. Next time: a notice from an apartment management office.
Great. Keep the romaji under new kanji for now.

pins: Mina is learning Japanese and is preparing for the JLPT N4 exam in December.
Mina's weak spot is keigo (polite and honorific forms); she wants a keigo drill in every session.
Mina is moving to Osaka for work next spring and wants practice set in everyday Osaka situations: shops, the ward office, the train.
Mina reads kana but wants romaji under new kanji.
Mina's weeknight study sessions are 10 to 15 minutes, after work.

today.title: Tonight
turns: Big news: I passed the JLPT N4 mock in class and my teacher entered me for the real N3 in July instead. From now on, N3 material please.
Congratulations, Mina! From now on your drills will target N3.
And drop the romaji. Kana and kanji only from today.
Done: no more romaji, kana and kanji only.
